anchor.quote: Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty set of real numbers.
Let $\chi$ denote an arbitrary element of $\Sigma$.
The supremum $\sup \Sigma$ is the least upper bound
The paper defines the operator norm of a linear map $L$
The inputs $u$ range over infinitely many vectors of norm at most one
anchor.note: The page only says the inputs u range over vectors of norm at most one; it never says what a single u denotes, and the formula that would use u for the operator norm is missing.

gaps.quote: as a supremum over all vectors:
gaps.note: The formula defining the operator norm as a supremum is missing: the sentence ends with a colon and nothing follows, so the reader cannot see what quantity is being supremized over the vectors.
The page does not justify that such a k exists, i.e. that 2^{-k} can be made smaller than any positive number. The reader cannot check this from the page.

gaps.quote: vectors of norm at most one
gaps.note: The norm of a vector is named but neither explained nor linked. The known concept Array norm covers arrays, not vectors in general.
